title: Security assessment runbook and evidence map
content:
Purpose:
This document is an operational runbook for responding to customer security questionnaires and trusts requests. It focuses on mapping typical questionnaire items to producible evidence (RBAC v2 artifacts, audit log extracts, SIEM export samples), describing an evidence automation pattern, and providing a repeatable SLA-driven workflow for the security + solutions team.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to inbound security questionnaires, RFP security sections, SOC2/ISO pre-sales Qs and short form customer checks.
- Not a policy; references policy artifacts and production configs.
- Assumes access to the evidence-exporter service (see linked artifacts) and readonly access to the Audit Log S3 bucket and RBAC metadata service.

High-level SLA and roles:
- Triage: Solutions Engineer (owner) — initial classification within 24 hours.
- Evidence gather: Product Security engineer — 3 business days for typical 50 question questionnaires if evidence is automated, 7–10 days if manual items or legal review required.
- Legal review: Legal lead — as scheduled, typical 2–3 business days on non-standard disclosures.
- Final packaging and delivery: Solutions Engineer — deliver to customer portal / drive and close ticket.

Triage checklist (first 24 hrs):
1) Record request source, customer, and deadline in JIRA.
2) Classify each question as: automated-evidence | canned-answer | requires-manual-collection | legal-review.
3) Mark items that are time-sensitive to operations (incident-related, PII access).
4) For automated-evidence items, flag required exporter(s): RBAC-metadata, Audit-log-extract, SIEM-sample, Config-snapshot.

Evidence mapping (common question -> artifact):
- "Describe role-based access controls for the platform" -> RBAC v2 design doc (rbac-v2-spec.md), example role JSON export, role-permission matrix CSV.
- "How are admin actions logged and retained?" -> audit-log schema doc, sample audit log extract (last 90 days), retention config snippet (S3 lifecycle policy).
- "Do you export logs to customer SIEM?" -> SIEM export config doc, sample exported event with field mapping, example ingestion manifest.
- "How do you handle key management and encryption at rest?" -> KMS integration diagram, CMK usage report, encryption-at-rest statement.
- "Can you provide evidence of user access reviews?" -> Quarterly access review summary (redacted), audit trail of review approvals, tickets for remediation.

Key artifacts and where to pull them from:
- RBAC metadata export: RBAC service -> /api/v2/roles/export (CSV/JSON). Evidence-exporter automation can run this and store output in staging S3.
- Audit log extracts: Audit logs (s3://redwood-audit-prod) -> run audit-extract job with query parameters (start,end,event_types,actor_id). Output: newline-delimited JSON.
- SIEM export sample: Pull last successful delivery manifest from SIEM delivery bucket (s3://siem-exports/prod/). Provide sample event + mapping doc.
- Config snapshots: Terraform state export + console snapshots for key controls (network, KMS, logging).

Audit log schema (approved summary for customer responses):
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of event.
- request_id: unique per request (traceable to distributed trace).
- actor_id: internal user or service account id.
- actor_role: primary role assignment at time of event (from RBAC v2 snapshot).
- event_type: normalized action (e.g., AUTHZ.GRANT, MODEL.INFER, CONFIG.UPDATE).
- resource: resource identifier (model id, route id, org id).
- client_ip: source IP (redacted if required).
- outcome: SUCCESS | FAILURE | DENIED.
- payload_hash: sha256 of relevant payload for integrity lookup.
- trace_id: optional tracing identifier linking to distributed trace.
- metadata: freeform context string (redacted as needed).

Notes about the schema: we never expose raw payloads for requests involving customer PII. For customer-facing samples, we redact client_ip and payload fields and provide a mapping that shows redaction rules. Retention: production default 7 years for immutable audit events; searchable indices retained 90 days.

SIEM export guidance (short):
- Export delivers NDJSON slices zipped with manifest indicating earliest_ts, latest_ts, events_count.
- Field mapping provided in manifest: e.g., siem.event_time -> timestamp, siem.actor.identifier -> actor_id, siem.action -> event_type.
- Delivery modes: push (HTTP webhook) or pull (S3 presigned). For customer-managed SIEM/private deployments we recommend S3 push + signing.

Evidence automation pattern (how we reduce manual work):
1) Maintain a small catalog of common question types and mapping to exporter jobs.
2) Evidence-exporter service (GHPR linked above) runs jobs against RBAC API, Audit S3, and Terraform state to produce standardized artifacts and a package.json manifest describing what was produced.
3) Automated redaction rules applied as a post-process (PII patterns, IP ranges).
4) A human reviewer validates the package and attaches legal signoffs when necessary.
5) Final artifacts uploaded to secure customer portal link with expiration.

Runbook: step-by-step for a new questionnaire
- Step 0: Create JIRA ticket and link questionnaire PDF/doc.
- Step 1: Triage and classify each question (use classification checklist).
- Step 2: For each automated item, add exporter job to JIRA subtask using evidence-exporter templates.
- Step 3: Run exporters, collect outputs to staging bucket.
- Step 4: Apply redaction + transform; generate manifest and canned answer snippets.
- Step 5: Security engineer reviews artifacts, marks any items for legal review.
- Step 6: Legal reviews flagged items, returns comments.
- Step 7: Package final deliverable (PDF + zip code of artifacts) and upload to secure link; post response in customer ticket.
- Step 8: Close loop: add internal retrospective note (what required manual work), update automation templates.

Canned answer snippets (examples to speed responses):
- Access control (short): "We enforce role-based access control (RBAC v2). Roles are defined centrally, assigned via least privilege, and changes are audited. Role definitions and assignment snapshots can be exported on request."
- Audit logging (short): "All control-plane and admin actions are logged to an immutable audit store. Logs include timestamp, actor_id, action, resource, and outcome. Logs are retained per our retention policy and can be exported to customer SIEMs under agreed terms."
- SIEM export (short): "We support export to customer SIEMs via S3 or secure push. Exports include normalized fields and a manifest documenting mapping; PII is redacted by default unless a separate agreement is in place."

Quality gates and redaction checklist for reviewers:
- Ensure no raw customer data appears in exported request payloads.
- Mask IPs and user emails unless explicitly requested and approved by Data Protection Officer.
- Confirm roles in RBAC export match the date of the request (include snapshot timestamp).
- Validate that retention statements reference published policy IDs.

Unresolved questions / decision items (for product-security):
- Do we standardize export retention for customer-delivered artifacts? (proposal: 30 days staging, 365 days archive)
- Should we provide a customer self-serve SIEM manifest generator in Console? (work item for product team).
- Legal: confirm exact phrasing allowed for "retention 7 years" in customer-facing doc.

Next steps / action items:
- (Asha) Finish templates for evidence-exporter jobs for RBAC and audit log extracts (JIRA-INF-8421).
- (Diego) Add SIEM manifest format examples to the exporter repo (PR #57).
- (Renee) Draft the customer-facing trust center entry that describes export capabilities + redaction.

Appendix: quick links and snippets
- RBAC v2 design doc: confluence://rbac-v2-design (internal)
- Audit log schema canonical: confluence://audit-log-schema-v1
- Evidence exporter repo: github.com/redwood-inference/security/evidence-exporter
- Example command to extract audit slice: 
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-scripts/audit-extract.py ./ && python audit-extract.py --start 2024-09-01 --end 2024-10-01 --types AUTHZ.GRANT --out out.ndjson

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an iterative working doc. Add any missing question patterns you see from customer questionnaires to the "catalog" section in the exporter repo.
- Keep canned answers short and point customers to the Trust Center for full policy text.

End of document.
